citations.review_text:
Was looking through my steam library for something new and decided to give this game a try, since I knew it had very positive reviews.

Good lord was it a disappointing experience, this game does not hold up in 2026.

The keybinds feel weird, the models look a little jank and the monsters just don't feel super animated. I get it's a story driven game but every encounter is just hard coded to have a certain outcome so there's no real sense of agency in the game.

The guns also just feel really terrible. Don't be deceived by the good reviews, this game is not worth your time.

ALSO, when they give you your loadout to go into the Polis tunnel (literally like the 3rd time you fight enemies), you have to HOLD the interact key to pick up your gun but every other time you press interact it's just a press, I thought my game broke and I had to look it up on a steam forum??? Unacceptable to be having these kinds of bugs on a 12 year old game.

Holy crap this game does NOT hold up. Enjoyed it back in the day but I had to uninstall after 15 minutes. The animations...haha...its like PS2 era at best seeing the monster do a a goofy ass tactical roll that looks so stiff. Its so clunky and slow you feel like you are a 300 pound activist. Just read the book instead. Also it runs insanely hot and poorly for a game that looks so bad and over a decade old. You find out within 15 minutes that the guns dont even feel good to shoot, at all.

Slow, boring, aweful gunplay, aged poorly. A remake could help but I just don't think its worth the time or money. 

It's punishing like a souls game and does not reward exploring every option. Consider looking up things before moving on to new zones or interacting with NPCs because the game will punish you for being both curious and not.

This game is like a more palatable version of Stalker. The shooting is really polished, which was unexpected. Combat encounters with human enemies & mutants feels good. The story and characters are interesting. Artyom's writes notes throughout the game giving you insight into his head space. 

There was only one time the game annoyed me. When following Khan, there's a point where he stops in a train and just stands there and says nothing. I did everything but what the game wanted from me. I was stuck for like 15mins. The game wants the player to Burn the Spider-Webs in front of Khan with the Lighter. If you don't know what to do Khan just stands there.   

Besides that the entire game is really good
Metro is a underrated gem.
Literally cant progress game 2 hours into campaign because bourbon wont move, waste of my time.

This suffers from the same general problem that STALKER suffers from, in that the actual challenge is not the stealth, the ammo conservation, or any actual challenge the game is supposed to have. The REAL challenge is in dealing with bad programming. Multiple game crashes, enemies who were already dead respawning after an autosave, and mandatory shooting gallery style levels with no healing causing repeated deaths over and over due to autosave sticking you in a situation where one hit will kill you and enemies can attack you through walls, game breaking soft-locks, infintely respawing enemies in a tunnel that no part of the game explains that you, the random stranger who just walked in, need to not only FIND but also PLANT a bomb to blow up a tunnel

I like challenge. I like to overcome adversity. But it still needs to be FUN. This isn't fun, it's just a buggy grind

claims.claim: The game provides a diegetic navigation system utilizing a compass and a lighter flame to show the objective direction.

citations.review_text:
I bought this game many years ago and just had it sitting on Steam. I finally got around to play it. 
Survival horror video games are not really my thing but I still recommend this game for people who enjoy this genre.
The campaign took me about 6 hours to complete and it did not really click with me. Sometimes, I don't know where to go and I cannot shoot with the compass in my hand. The compass points to the main objective which causes you to sometimes miss a bonus objective. Even in Spartan mode (that should have more ammo available), I found myself running low on ammo many times (maybe my aim is bad but it felt annoying).

Metro's atmosphere and immersion are unmatched. The king of diagetic gameplay. for example, don't know where to go? use your compass(North is always where you need to go) or pop open your lighter(the flame tilts in the direction you need to go). The gas mask cracks, the watch counts down the time left on a filter, it's great. The story is good, I personally love the atmosphere thick with toska, radiation, and darkness. Only thing negatively I can say about the story is the morality system is rather obscure. Gameplay is fun, although some things are a little janky, such as what makes the librarians attack or back off, and stealth in general. overall, a great linear singleplayer game in the age of open world games

claims.claim: Reviewers report that core mechanics such as gas filters, battery charging, and using the lighter are left unexplained to new players.

citations.review_text:
Metro 2033 Redux was my first introduction to the Metro franchise and honestly, it was confusing. The game throws you into a post-apocalyptic Moscow with barely any explanation and expects you to understand the different references, mutants, the Dark Ones, psychic visions and whatever the ♥♥♥♥ is going on with Artyom

The atmosphere is also really good. The underground sections are dark, claustrophobic and genuinely uncomfortable, especially when you don't know what's waiting around the next corner. The surface sections are even better because they show just how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the world became after the nuclear war

The gameplay is solid. Ammo and resources are limited, so you actually have to think about what you're using instead of shooting everything that moves. The gas mask and filter system is also a good addition, especially during the surface sections. The gunplay isn't anything incredible, but it fits the survival focused gameplay quite well

My biggest problem is the story. It's interesting once you understand it, but the game does a pretty poor job of explaining itself to a new player. I spent a good portion of the game wondering what the hell was going on. Then the Dark Ones show up and Artyom starts having visions, making it even harder to tell what's real and whats not. What doesn't help either is the player not being taught about the different mechanics implemented, I found myself googling or looking at binds constantly to do certain things 

A minor thing to note, Steam overlay did not work for 90% of my time spent in-game for some reason 

Overall, solid experience. Will dive further into the franchise whenver I get the chance

very dark and gritty game. the atmosphere and immersion fills you with dread with having to manage resources and filters. monsters are very scary. good story and characters, the game becomes much more terrifying when you're all alone and all your allies are missing or dead.

however the gameplay has some issues on the hardest difficulty, for some reason during one of the missions where you fight a bunch of nazis in a tunnel the checkpoints just stop appearing halfway throughout the mission. the mission where you face a bunch of monsters that you have to stare at to stop them from killing you is terribly designed, you have to stare at the monsters for literally minutes to stop them from attacking you, and sometimes the AI is buggy so they kill you instantly anyways. killing them is pointless because they need 100 bullets + grenades to kill them and they one shot you as well. finally, many game mechanics were unexplained, such as the gas filters, battery, and using your lighter to burn spiderwebs.

overall decent spooky game, similar to wolfenstein but with more horror aspects.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features diegetic mechanics such as a gas mask with cracking visuals, replaceable filters with timer watches, and a manual flashlight pump.

citations.review_text: It’s unbelievable how Metro 2033 Redux still completely blows modern shooters out of the water. Games from 12 to 16 years ago rarely felt this immersive. The tactile survival mechanics—having to manually wipe condensation off your gas mask, watch filter timers tick down, hand-pump your flashlight, and treat military-grade bullets as actual currency—create a level of tension that modern AAA games struggle to replicate. Combined with eerie lighting and unforgettable underground world-building, it isn't just a classic; it's a timeless masterclass in survival horror.

Don't get me wrong, I'll talk a lot about what I prefered in the book, but the game is INSANELY good, it has aged but it is still completely playable and enjoyable, but the book is some kind of another level to me.

I get it that it was the original release was in the era of action shooter game, so I understand that it's way more action based than the novel. I think that a Walking Sim game would actually be better to fully depict the book.

Gameplay wise, it's very good for its age. There are depth in the system, the gas mask, flashlight, the different weapons, the stealth mecanism, the currency that can be used as ammo, overall the ressource management is a big win.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering random crashes and chapter-breaking bugs during gameplay.

citations.review_text:
One of the best post-apocalyptic games out there. Graphics and atmosphere are amazing, story-wise it's deep and sad, but you can truly learn something, especially with the way you play and interact with the world. You really do reap what you sow.
The only things that threw me off were a few random crashes here and there, and also a few chapter-breaking bugs, that are pretty common from what I read online. Other than that, this game is a beautiful experience.

Metro Redux 2033 is a journey through the metro of a devastated Moscow manages to immerse in an oppressive world, where the stations function as small societies opposed to each other and the tunnels are full of mutants, human factions and threats that often feel more unsettling for what they suggest than for what they show, the combination of survival, horror, exploration, stealth and combat works especially well when the game forces you to manage ammunition, mask filters and resources, making every outing to the surface or incursion into an abandoned tunnel carry real tension, the story does not rely solely on big cinematic scenes, many of the best moments are in the ambient conversations, the living conditions inside the stations and the small details that make you feel this world continues to exist beyond Artyom, however, the game loses points for its lack of technical polish.
Despite some texture issues, unexpected crashes, and environmental glitches—like stairs that behave strangely and cause unfair damage or death—the game's strengths far outweigh its flaws. These technical problems aren't isolated, as others have reported crashes when loading saves or reaching certain points. Additionally, inconsistent AI, physics, and stealth detection can occasionally break the otherwise strong immersion. 

Even so, the exceptional atmosphere, distinct art direction, and engaging story about fear and survival make it a memorable experience. While technical errors hold it back from a higher score, better stability and polish could easily push it into the 9 range.

After multiple play trough’s, I find myself just quitting the game because I have seen the long cut scene videos too many times already. I don’t care about the wedding, or the mission panning after the first time playing it because they are so long, and you cannot skip them. Honestly I hated them the first time I played the game. One other thing! Why can’t the keyboard layout be the same throughout the game? I have to switch to the default layout just to get through the cut scenes and other annoying things and then switch it back to how I play afterwards.
pretty darn good. although the cut scenes can be a bit of a bother, beside that this nails the apocalypse vibe perectly.

Nota Geral | Overall Rating
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]Metro 2033 é sobre atmosfera antes de qualquer outra coisa, e é nisso que o jogo é praticamente insuperável. A 4A Games construiu um mundo pós-apocalíptico opressor, sujo e desesperador, onde cada túnel do metrô de Moscou parece guardar um perigo diferente. É um jogo que não tem medo de te deixar desconfortável, seja pela escassez de munição, pela escuridão sufocante ou pelos horrores que espreitam na superfície irradiada. Não é um shooter no sentido tradicional, é uma experiência de sobrevivência disfarçada de FPS, e essa combinação funciona de um jeito que poucos jogos conseguiram replicar depois.[/b]

[i]Metro 2033 is about atmosphere before anything else, and that's where the game is nearly unmatched. 4A Games built an oppressive, filthy, and desperate post-apocalyptic world, where every tunnel of the Moscow metro seems to hide a different danger. It's a game unafraid of making you uncomfortable, whether through ammo scarcity, suffocating darkness, or the horrors lurking on the irradiated surface. It's not a traditional shooter, it's a survival experience disguised as an FPS, and that combination works in a way few games managed to replicate afterward.[/i]

Jogabilidade | Gameplay
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]O sistema de munição militar como moeda é uma das melhores decisões de design do jogo: cada bala boa que você usa em combate é dinheiro que você não vai ter para comprar equipamento depois. Isso cria uma tensão constante em cada troca de tiro, te forçando a decidir entre gastar munição de qualidade ou economizar com a munição fraca, feita em casa. O uso da máscara de gás, que embaça, racha e precisa ser trocada, e a lanterna manual, que precisa ser recarregada fisicamente, são detalhes que reforçam a vulnerabilidade do protagonista o tempo todo. O combate contra humanos é tático e recompensa furtividade, enquanto os confrontos contra mutantes na superfície são caóticos e genuinamente assustadores.[/b]

Most post-apocalyptic games give you a feeling of “adventure”.
But Metro 2033 is not like that, it feels more like a suffocating long night train ride.
[h3] Dark, confined, terrifying, oppressive, endless. [/h3]

Most of the game’s story takes place deep inside the metro tunnels.
An underground world beneath the surface.
The environment is almost always pitch black.
You can barely see what’s ahead, and danger is everywhere — mutated creatures lurk in every tunnel.

The game fully captures the feeling of nuclear apocalypse.
Even when you reach the surface, there is no “breathing space”.
You are met with ruins, mutated creatures, and a nuclear winter that wraps everything in cold silence.

There is a very special system in this game:
[b] Bullets are currency. [/b]
Bullets come in two types:
1: Homemade standard rounds
2: Military-grade rounds left from the old world (which also function as money)
The second type is both ammunition and currency.

If you play in survival mode, resources become extremely tight.
I often ended up in situations where I simply ran out of bullets.
In that complete darkness, the tension becomes extremely intense.
Once your homemade ammo is gone, you can switch to military rounds, but when those are gone too, you lose both your firepower and your “buying power”, and can only rely on scavenging.

Weapon systems further strengthen this survival pressure.
Pneumatic weapons require manual pumping to maintain pressure.
Gas masks can break. Filter cartridges have time limits.
You are constantly “maintaining your own survival state”.

What’s more interesting is humanity itself.
Humanity destroyed the surface world with war, yet continues repeating history underground.
Different factions form inside metro stations, and eventually evolve into forms of “authoritarian metro regimes”, constantly fighting each other again.
